copies.headline: Kaleb's 6-4 Is a Magic Trick
copies.body:
The record says 6-4, the all-play says 40-70 and last in scoring at 103.2. Kaleb has banked +2.4 wins he didn't earn, and this is the week the bill arrives. The backfield is the gap: Jeanty and Hall at 14 and 13 against Kenneth Walker III (26) and Bucky Irving (17), with Rico Dowdle and Kimani Vidal behind them if Walker's questionable tag goes bad. Kaleb has nothing behind Jeanty and Hall — Harvey is on IR. Tight end is another six points the wrong way, Mayer in a Raiders offense that's a 10-point dog with a 40.5 total.
The receiver room is where it really rots: Tate and McConkey both questionable, Addison out, London and Concepcion at zero. Tate is the ceiling, and Titans-Cowboys at 55.5 is the only shootout Kaleb owns. Adam gets Olave chasing in New Orleans' 11.5-point loss and Loveland on the other side of that 48.5.

copies.headline: Logan's Receivers Outclass Noah's Entire Roster
copies.body:
This is decided at wide receiver, where Logan's top three project 49 to Noah's 38, and the gap is wider than the number. Justin Jefferson gets a 45.5 total in San Francisco with Minnesota taking points, Luther Burden sits in a 48.5-point game Chicago is favored to control, and Tetairoa McMillan draws Baltimore in a competitive 43.5. Noah's answer is Garrett Wilson in a 41.5-total slog at the Chargers, plus Jaylen Waddle and Jordyn Tyson both carrying questionable tags — and Waddle's Denver game has the week's lowest total at 40.5. Behind them: Josh Downs and Ja'Kobi Lane. That's not depth, that's a waiting room.
Noah's one real edge is running back, 28 to 23, and even that leans on James Cook in a game Buffalo is favored by 16.5 with a 45.5 total — great for carries, bad for garbage-time volume if it's 31-7 by the third. Logan also wins quarterback with Joe Burrow in a 54.5 shootout at Washington and tight end with Isaiah Likely. Logan is the #3 power ranking at 122.7 a game and is minus-two wins on luck; Noah is last in all-play at 34 percent.

copies.headline: John's Receiver Room Can't Cover Lamb
copies.body:
Two 5-5 teams with identical all-play records and identical bad luck, and the separator is obvious: wide receiver. John's best three project 35, and that's Tee Higgins plus Xavier Hutchinson and Malik Washington, which is one real player and two guys you'd rather not say out loud. Puka Nacua is on IR and nothing behind him moves the needle. Christian's top three go 47, headlined by CeeDee Lamb in a 55.5-point Dallas game against Tennessee — the fattest total on the slate. Twelve points of edge at one position is usually the whole game.
John answers at running back, and it's a real answer: Jonah Coleman in a Denver blowout and D'Andre Swift with Chicago laying 11.5, though a 40.5 total caps Coleman's ceiling. But Christian has Chase Brown in a 54.5-point Bengals game and five viable backs if Bhayshul Tuten's questionable tag sticks. John has none of that insurance.

copies.headline: Leif's Receivers Can't Cover Ja'Marr Chase
copies.body:
This is a wideout mismatch and nothing else really closes it. Isaac's top three — Ja'Marr Chase in a 54.5-total game at Washington, Malik Nabers with the Giants getting six at home, and a questionable Jakobi Meyers — project 52 against Leif's 35, and Leif's room is held together with tape: Davante Adams on IR, Mike Evans questionable, and Stefon Diggs as the WR1 by default. Backfields wash at 34 apiece, Josh Allen over C.J. Stroud is a two-point nudge, and T.J. Hockenson gives Isaac the tight end edge if his tag clears. Dalton Kincaid is the fallback, which is more than Leif has behind Dalton Schultz.
The game environments favor Isaac too. Buffalo laying 16.5 with a 45.5 total is the classic Allen-sits-in-the-third script, and Houston minus 12.5 in a 43.5 game caps Schultz and David Montgomery. Leif is 7-3 on 2.3 wins of luck with a 64.7 still on the ledger. Power rankings have him ninth for a reason.

copies.headline: Grant's Depth Buries Mitchell's Top-Heavy Three
copies.body:
The top-line numbers say this is a coin flip — 22 and 22 at quarterback, 31 to 30 at running back — so it gets decided at receiver and in the back half of the lineup. Grant's best three (Amon-Ra St. Brown, Zay Flowers, Caleb Douglas) project 42 to Mitchell's 38, and Mitchell's margin for error there is nonexistent: behind Nico Collins and DJ Moore it's Treylon Burks and a zeroed-out Matthew Golden, with Christian Kirk on IR. Grant at least has Christian Watson as a warm body. Douglas is questionable, which is the one crack in that edge.
Game script helps Grant too. Tennessee is an 8.5-point dog in a 55.5-point game, which is Tony Pollard catching passes in the fourth quarter, and Baltimore being a road underdog at Carolina keeps Flowers busy. Mitchell's leverage is Jahmyr Gibbs in a 43.5-total Detroit game they're favored to control, plus Dak Prescott in that same Dallas shootout. That's a real ceiling, but it's three players carrying ten roster spots. Grant's floor is higher in more places.

copies.headline: Peter's Backfield Is An Empty Room
copies.body:
This is a running back mismatch dressed up as a .500 showdown. CJ rolls out Chuba Hubbard against Baltimore in a 43.5-total game Carolina is favored in, plus Jonathan Taylor, who will get 25 touches even as a 12.5-point dog in Houston because Indy has no other plan. Peter counters with Kyle Monangai and Emari Demercado while Bijan Robinson sits and Josh Jacobs is out — a 20-point hole at the position before anyone touches the ball. The receiver room is worse: George Pickens in a 55.5-total Dallas game is legitimate, but Adonai Mitchell is the WR2 and A.J. Brown is questionable with nothing behind him.
Peter's path is narrow and known. He needs Brock Bowers to clear his questionable tag and feast in a garbage-time Raiders loss, Pickens to go for 25, and Rodgers to actually produce in a 37.5-total slog in Philadelphia. That's three things breaking right against a team that only needs two. CJ's floor — Hubbard, Taylor, Parker Washington against the Giants, Rashee Rice in a 15.5-point Kansas City blowout — is simply higher than Peter's ceiling most weeks.

intro: Adam gets Kaleb with first place on the line, and it's the rare top-three meeting where the favorite still has to sweat — Kaleb's a win away from taking the whole thing over. Leif's the other 7-3 team and he's the one drawing an underdog tag at home against Isaac, which is what happens when half your lineup is listed as questionable on a Friday. The rest of the slate is five teams at 5-5 trying to avoid the part of November where the playoff math starts requiring help from Noah and Mitchell.
